_note: Names of the menu item numbers of the user menu (number -> {name, status, flags, sub_elements}). The file stores 0x06000000 plus the number. 'flags' = IDs of the flags of the file that are 1 for the sub-elements of the item that were switched on when it was added, in the order of 'sub_elements' (the dialog of the camera); only given where known. 'sub_flags' (optional) = the flags of the sub-elements in the order of 'sub_elements' where 'flags' has more entries.

1101.name: ISO/Gain/EI
1101.evidence: FS7M2 user menu file DEFG, second version (2026-10-21): ISO/Gain/EI added as the 14th item changed slot 00014 from 0,0 to 100664397,0 (= 0x06000000 + 1101) and eight flags from 0 to 1: 01203 to 01207 and 01271 to 01273. The camera asks which sub-elements to take along when an item is added (they can be switched on and off one by one): the flags are that selection. Third version (2026-10-21): deselecting the first sub-element in the camera dialog switched exactly one flag off, 01207: so 01207 is the first sub-element . Fourth version: first sub-element switched on again, second one off: only 01203 went 1 -> 0 (and 01207 back to 1): the second sub-element is 01203, so the dialog order does not follow the flag numbers (01207, 01203, ...). Order of the sub-elements in the camera dialog (user, 2026-10-21): Mode, ISO/Gain <H>, ISO/Gain <M>, ISO/Gain <L>, Exposure Index <H>, Exposure Index <M>, Exposure Index <L>, Shockless Gain. Confirmed: Mode = 01207, ISO/Gain <H> = 01203; the other six flags (01204, 01205, 01206, 01271, 01272, 01273) are only partly assigned: sub-elements 3, 5 and 7 (ISO/Gain <M>, Exposure Index <H>, Exposure Index <L>) switched off together turned 01204, 01271 and 01273 off (all others stayed on), so these three flags belong to 3, 5, 7 in an order not yet known (likely 01204 = 3, 01271 = 5, 01273 = 7). Sixth version (sub-elements 4, 5 and 8 off, and every other item deleted from the user menu): against the version with all eight on, 01205, 01206 and 01271 went to 0. Together with the 3-5-7 file (01204, 01271, 01273): sub-element 5 (Exposure Index <H>) = 01271 (in both sets); 01272 is the only flag in neither set = sub-element 6; 3 and 7 are 01204 / 01273 in unknown order, 4 and 8 are 01205 / 01206 in unknown order. Deleting the other thirteen items from the user menu changed no flag: the camera keeps the sub-element flags of an item after it is taken out. Seventh version (6, 7, 8 off, only ISO/Gain/EI in the menu): 01206, 01272 and 01273 went to 0. All three sets together decide every sub-element: Mode 01207, ISO/Gain <H> 01203, ISO/Gain <M> 01204, ISO/Gain <L> 01205, Exposure Index <H> 01271, Exposure Index <M> 01272, Exposure Index <L> 01273, Shockless Gain 01206 (the list 'flags' is in the order of the sub-elements).

474.name: Focus
474.evidence: FS7M2 user menu file DEFG, thirteenth version (2026-10-21): slot 1 changed from ND Filter to Focus: 00001 = 100663770,0 (= 0x06000000 + 474) and 14 flags from 0 to 1 (all three sub-elements Focus Area, Focus Area (Push AF) and AF Assist selected in the camera dialog): 00571 to 00574, 00670, 00757 to 00759, 00775 to 00777, 01310, 01904 and 01905 (01310, 01904 and 01905 exist only in FS7M2 files). Several flags per sub-element: which flags belong to which sub-element is not isolated yet (no sub_elements entry until it is). Fourteenth version: Focus Area deselected: only 00670 went 1 -> 0, so Focus Area = 00670 (one flag); the other 13 flags belong to Focus Area (Push AF) and AF Assist (or are not sub-element flags). Fifteenth version: Focus Area (Push AF) deselected (against the version with all three on): only 01904 went 1 -> 0, so Focus Area (Push AF) = 01904. AF Assist is not isolated yet (candidate: 01905); the other twelve flags (00571-00574, 00757-00759, 00775-00777, 01310) stayed on when either sub-element was deselected. Sixteenth version: AF Assist deselected: only 01905 went 1 -> 0, so AF Assist = 01905. All three sub-elements have one flag each (00670, 01904, 01905); the other eleven flags (00571-00574, 00757-00759, 00775-00777, 01310) stay on whichever sub-element is deselected: they come on with the item (flags of the item itself), 'flags' holds all fourteen, 'sub_flags' the three of the sub-elements.
